a:r.a:t: Formation of the First Peptide Bond

p:cNvPr.descr: An image of the second elongation step in bacteria: formation of the first peptide bond. On the bottom left is the same image as the last image in fig 27-29. Above this is an inset box. On the top left is an enlarged version of the blue fMet circle. This begins with C, which double bonds left to O, bonds up to H and down to N, which bonds down to H and right to C, which bonds up to R1, down to H, and right to C, which double bonds up to O. A red arrow points from this bond line back up to O. C also bonds down to O, which bonds down to the top left of an inverted pentagon with thick top sides. The top right point bonds up to HO, the right point bonds down, then bottom middle point is O, and the bottom left point bonds down, then left to O, which has a dashed line below leading to P site. On the right is an enlarged version of the AA2 circle, where N bonds up to H, down to H and right to C. The N has two red dots on the left with a red arrow on the left pointing to the C on the right side of fMet. C in AA2 bonds up to R2, down to H and right to C, which double bonds up to O and bonds down to O, which has a replica of the pentagon just described, but the O with the dash going down does not lead to anything. This is labeled as the A site. To the right of this box is a right arrow pointing to another box that is a replica of the first, but the left pentagon’s right upper point bonds up to O, which bonds up to H. The C on the right side that bonds up to O. A red arrow points from this O back to its bond line. The bond line from the right C down to O has a red arrow pointing down to the H on the top right point of the pentagon. There is also an arrow from this bond line pointing to the bottom left H of AA2. An arrow points from the N down to H bond and points back to N. To the right of this is an arrow pointing to a larger box, which has the fMet circle enlarged with its molecular structure bonded on top of the AA2 circle, which sits on the A site. Below this is the P site with an arrow pointing to the E site. From the image on the bottom left is an arrow pointing right to a replica of itself, only the fMet circle is bonded on top of the AA2 circle. This arrow is identified as the peptide formation bond.
